Suppose $f(x),g(x),h(x)$ and $k(x)$ are functions and $c$ is a nonzero constant. Then, we have the following properties of Big-O notation.

- The sum and product properties. If

$$
f=O(h)\,\text{and}\,g=O(k)\,\text{as}\,x\to a,
$$

then

$$
f+g=O(h+k)\,\text{and}\,fg=O(hk)\,\text{as}\,x\to a.
$$

- The constant multiple property. If

$$
f=O(cg)\,\text{as}\,x\to a,
$$

then

$$
f=O(g)\,\text{as}\,x\to a.
$$

- The reflexive property.

$$
f=O(f)\,\text{as}\,x\to a.
$$

- The transitive property. If

$$
f=O(g)\,\text{and}\,g=O(h)\,\text{as}\,x\to a,
$$

then

$$
f=O(h)\,\text{as}\,x\to a.
$$

- The absorption property. If

$$
f=O(g+h)\,\text{and}\,g=O(h)\,\text{as}\,x\to a,
$$

then

$$
f=O(h)\,\text{as}\,x\to a.
$$

With that in mind, let us justify each selected step.

- We first consider line $\text{L1},$ which states that

$$
2{e}^{4x}=O(2{e}^{4x}),
$$

and this follows by $\text{the reflexive property}.$

- Next, we consider line $\text{L4}.$ From line $\text{L1}$ we have

$$
2{e}^{4x}=O(2{e}^{4x}),
$$

and from line $\text{L3}$ we have

$$
x=O(2{e}^{4x}).
$$

Since $f=2{e}^{4x}+x,$ by lines $\text{L1 and L3}$ and $\text{the sum property},$ we obtain

$$
f=2{e}^{4x}+x=O(2{e}^{4x}+2{e}^{4x})=O(4{e}^{4x}),
$$

which justifies line $\text{L4}.$

- Finally, we consider line $\text{L5}.$ From line $\text{L4}$ we have

$$
f=O(4{e}^{4x}),
$$

and by $\text{the constant multiple property}$ with $c=4,$ we conclude

$$
f=O({e}^{4x}).
$$
html:
Suppose f(x),g(x),h(x) and k(x) are functions and c is a nonzero constant. Then, we have the following properties of Big-O notation.

  • The sum and product properties. If
    f=O(h)andg=O(k)asx→a, then
    f+g=O(h+k)andfg=O(hk)asx→a.

  • The constant multiple property. If
    f=O(cg)asx→a, then
    f=O(g)asx→a.

  • The reflexive property.
    f=O(f)asx→a.

  • The transitive property. If
    f=O(g)andg=O(h)asx→a, then
    f=O(h)asx→a.

  • The absorption property. If
    f=O(g+h)andg=O(h)asx→a, then
    f=O(h)asx→a.

With that in mind, let us justify each selected step.

  • We first consider line L1, which states that
    2e4x=O(2e4x), and this follows by the reflexive property.

  • Next, we consider line L4. From line L1 we have
    2e4x=O(2e4x), and from line L3 we have
    x=O(2e4x). Since f=2e4x+x, by lines L1 and L3 and the sum property, we obtain
    f=2e4x+x=O(2e4x+2e4x)=O(4e4x), which justifies line L4.

  • Finally, we consider line L5. From line L4 we have
    f=O(4e4x), and by the constant multiple property with c=4, we conclude
    f=O(e4x).
